title: Transaction proxy for Optimize apply: dedup tokens, webhook gateway, and SDK primitives
creator: Ava Patel
description: Problem: Optimize suggestions that patch batching/caching configs must be applied safely to customer control planes. Current webhook flow (fire-and-forget) leads to duplicated or partial applies when retries, timeouts, or operator actions occur. Goal: provide an API + SDK + gateway pattern that enables exactly-once or well-defined at-most-once semantics for recommend->apply cycles while preserving the ability to safely rollback and reconcile. Non-goals: full distributed transactions across customer services; we will not change customer-side config formats.
technical_summary: Introduce a lightweight 'apply transaction proxy' service in Optimize control plane that brokers suggestion commits. It issues monotonic transaction IDs (tx_id), accepts 'prepare' RPCs, records idempotency tokens in a durable store, forwards a single webhook to the customer's receiver with tx metadata, and provides commit/abort endpoints consumed by SDK or webhook adapter. The proxy exposes both REST endpoints and an SDK helper for retries and local deduplication. Persistence uses RocksDB-backed store (or existing config DB) with TTLed tombstones. A DLQ and replay worker will handle failed commits. Observability and tracing are included for audit and SLA metrics.
design_decisions: Use a two-phase flow: prepare -> apply/commit -> ack to provide durable handoff without blocking long-running customer side operations.
Idempotency represented by client-supplied idempotency_token + server-issued tx_id; operations deduped by token within retention window.
Proxy records a lightweight proof-of-delivery (POD) record for each outbound webhook and transitions state with CAS to ensure single-flush semantics.
Rollback implemented as a compensating operation: the proxy supports an explicit 'revert' RPC that triggers customer revert webhook and internal reconciliation.
Avoid external distributed locks; instead rely on monotonic tx_ids and single-writer ordering per recommendation id.
Security: all calls require service token + per-transaction HMAC for webhook payload to prevent replay from untrusted actors.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes prepare_apply(commit_metadata) and commit_apply(tx_id) with transparent retry semantics; retries do not result in duplicate customer applies.
Webhook gateway only delivers a single outbound webhook per tx_id; repeated upstream prepare calls reuse existing tx_id and return stable status.
Proxy persists idempotency keys and pod records with TTL; records visible in Console trace for each apply attempt.
Rollback flow reverses configuration or records a revert event; reconciler worker can detect partial applies and either complete or enqueue revert tasks.
Unit + integration tests covering duplicate prepare, network partition, delayed commit, and DLQ replay scenarios.
Load test demonstrating proxy can handle 500 qps of prepare requests with median 10ms local latency (excluding outbound webhook latency) and bounded memory usage.
Security review completed and HMAC key rotation tested.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Schema + store (2 days) - define tx record schema, idempotency index, tombstone TTL. Phase 2: Proxy endpoints + SDK stub (5 days) - implement /v1/prepare, /v1/commit, /v1/abort and a Go/TS SDK helper. Phase 3: Webhook adapter (3 days) - add POD logic, outbound delivery with retries and DLQ. Phase 4: Reconciler & revert worker (4 days) - background worker that inspects stuck tx and reconciles. Phase 5: Tests + rollout (3 days) - e2e tests, canary rollout, console traces. Total estimate: ~17 workdays.
outstanding_risks: Retention window too short could allow duplicate replays after tombstone expiry; must pick conservative TTL and monitor storage growth.
Customer webhook receiver behavior is a black box; long-running apply handlers could cause many in-flight tx and increased resource pressure—must provide backoff strategies and advisory timeouts.
Proxy becomes single point of failure for applies: plan for HA (leader election + replica read-through) and fallback mode that reverts to best-effort webhook if proxy unavailable.
Auditability requirements may mandate additional metadata storage; budget and cost implications for long retention need alignment with privacy/compliance.

api_contract: Endpoints: POST /v1/apply/prepare {recommendation_id, idempotency_token, payload_meta} -> 202 {tx_id, status}, GET /v1/apply/status/{tx_id} -> 200 {status, attempts}, POST /v1/apply/commit {tx_id} -> 200, POST /v1/apply/abort {tx_id, reason} -> 200. Webhook: outbound includes headers X-Redwood-Tx: <tx_id>, X-Redwood-Signature: <hmac>. SDK: prepareApply(...), commitApply(txId), abortApply(txId) with exponential backoff and transparent dedup handling.
observability_and_alerts: Metrics: optimize.apply.prepare.count, optimize.apply.duplicate_prepare.count, optimize.apply.commit.latency, optimize.apply.dlq.count. Alerts: DLQ rate > 5/min for 5m, duplicate_prepare rate > 1% sustained, reconcile backfill > threshold. Traces: sample 1% of applies with full payload; make tx_id available as trace tag. Console: new 'Apply transactions' table with filter by recommendation_id and status timeline.
migration_and_rollout: Start behind feature flag. Run canary for 2 days on low-traffic customers and compare apply success and duplicate rates against baseline. If proxy unavailable, fallback to best-effort webhook and mark tx status as 'fallback' so reconciler can handle. Gradual ramp with 10/30/100% buckets.
testing_plan: Unit tests for idempotency store, integration tests against a fake customer receiver that simulates ACK/no-ACK and delayed ACK. Chaos test: drop outbound webhook 50% of the time to validate DLQ and replay. Load tests in staging with synthetic recommendation churn. Post-deploy smoke script to validate prepare->commit flow and verify traces in Console.
